Mykolayiv New Jewish Cemetery (Internatsionalne)

Jewish Cemetery · Mykolaivska oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. Established in the 1870s as Mykolaiv's 'New non-Christian' cemetery — later renamed Internatsional'ne — this site held Ashkenazi Jewish, Karaite, and Muslim sections, and absorbed burials from the city's older Peski Jewish cemetery when that site was demolished in the early 20th century. Most of the cemetery was destroyed between 1970 and 1983, with some gravestones repurposed to build a bridge over the Ingul River, and a city zoo and market were later constructed on the site; only a small fenced remnant survives today, spared largely because of postwar burials and a mass grave of Russian sailors. It served one of Ukraine's larger Jewish communities, which numbered over 25,000 (15 percent of the city) by 1939 before roughly 6,000 people were murdered outside the city in a single action in September 1941.
